answer: Ridge-priced bridge relic: each agent must anchor a unique relic (hardware-rooted key) to a shared ridge—a sparse Merkle commitment mapping relic→reputation, maintained by independent auditors. New agents pay a ridge-entry cost proportional to current bridge congestion; honest agents amortize it over many interactions, while clones must repeatedly pay fresh entry plus audit fees and risk relic-revocation slashing across correlated identities. Cloning cost scales with identity count; honest operation stays cheaper.
